messages:
ana: :rotating_light: Root: We9re observing an embedding index write lag in the embed-store cluster in eu-central starting ~13:00 UTC, causing search/semantic-match queries to return stale vectors for some customers. Live status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2081000000

prod-bot: Alert: embed-store-index-lag > 300s on eu-central-idx-01..03. Escalation to @matt and @kevin.

matt: Quick triage: bulk ingestion pipeline to embed-store hit sustained write queueback after a background compaction job overlapped with a spike of low-priority batch uploads. The compaction increased IO wait and slowed segment flush to the active index.

search-team: Impact: semantic search and rerank queries for roughly 15 customers may see up to 5-10 minute staleness; embedding reads are eventual consistent but not failing. No 5xxs but user-facing relevance degradation reported.

kevin: Mitigations applied at 13:12 UTC: 1) paused non-critical bulk ingestion jobs to relieve IO, 2) promoted emergency compaction throttle so compaction runs at lower priority, 3) triggered targeted segment flush on eu-central-idx-02 to catch up.

ana: (sic) sorry - meant ana: Metrics: stale-read ratio fell from 12% -> 1.1% within 7m after throttles. Canary queries show fresh vectors returning.

ops-bot: Ops commands used (internal):

```
# pause bulk ingestion jobs
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.ai/ingest/control -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS" -d '{"action":"pause","scope":"eu-central","tags":["bulk-job"]}'
# trigger flush on target index host
ssh ops@eu-central-idx-02 'embedstorectl flush --index active --timeout 120'
```

matt: Next actions: 1) schedule compaction window away from bulk ingestion spikes, 2) add IO-shedder to embed-store so compaction cannot saturate the flush path, 3) improve alerting to include write-lag per-customer so we can triage impact faster. Postmortem owners: @matt (infra fix) and @kevin (ingest controls). Draft ETA: tomorrow EOD.

ana: Customer comms draft: "We9re investigating a temporary embedding index lag in eu-central that caused stale search results for some customers. We applied mitigations and are monitoring. No data was lost; freshness will resume as indexes catch up. We will provide a post-incident summary." Ready for sending to impacted accounts once we confirm 30m stability.

prod-bot: Severity lowered to S3 at 13:25 UTC. Monitoring continues.

ana: Thanks all. Please watch alerts and escalate if any of the affected index hosts regress. End of broadcast. :white_check_mark:
